name: application-split-view-layout
title: Split View Layout
description: Resizable master-detail two-pane shell with a collapsible list side and a detail content slot, driven by a typed items/detail prop contract.
useWhen: Building an inbox, ticket queue, or document browser where selecting an item in a list updates a detail pane.
Users benefit from seeing the list and the currently open item simultaneously rather than navigating between pages.
The list side should be collapsible to give the detail pane more room on demand.
avoidWhen: You only need a generic resizable two-pane split with no list/detail semantics — use the plain Resizable component instead.
The interface is primarily mobile — a master-detail split doesn't fit narrow viewports; navigate between list and detail as separate screens instead.
There is only ever one detail view with no list to select from — a simple page layout is simpler than this shell.
responsiveBehavior: The two-pane layout assumes desktop-class width; below a breakpoint, replace the list+detail split with a single-pane navigation (list, then detail) rather than shrinking both columns.
accessibility: The resize handle uses role='separator' with aria-orientation='vertical' and a descriptive aria-label per the WAI-ARIA window-splitter pattern.
Each list item is a real <button> with aria-current marking the active selection, not just a background color change.
The collapse-list icon button carries an explicit aria-label since it shows only an icon.

variants.title: Split View Layout
variants.description: Inbox-style split view with a collapsible list pane, a resize handle, and a detail pane showing the selected item's content.
accessibility: The active list item sets aria-current='true' in addition to its background tint, so selection state is announced.

variants.title: Split View Layout (Dark)
variants.description: Master-detail split view adapted for dark surfaces with the same list, resize-handle, and detail-pane structure.
accessibility: List item text, the resize handle, and detail-pane content must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
